text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel has suspended the transport of lorries through the tunnel after a problem with the overhead electrical power supply, a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"We have suspended the service for HGVs (Heavy Goods Vehicles)," said a Eurotunnel spokeswoman. The lorry service is operating only on a test basis following a blaze in the tunnel last November.
One train was trapped in the tunnel for 30 minutes on Thursday morning following the initial power failure, the spokeswoman said.
Eurotunnel has been carrying lorries free of charge pending authorisation for a full resumption of freight traffic, which it hopes to receive by mid-June.
The spokeswoman said two trains per hour were running each way through the tunnel at the moment while engineers worked on the power supply problem.
Car passengers with prior bookings were being taken through the tunnel but those without reservations were being redirected towards the ferries.
